name: Vedolizumab
route_note: IV infusion at weeks 0, 2 and 6, then every 8 weeks; subcutaneous maintenance every 2 weeks

discovery.note: Humanised IgG1 version of the murine antibody Act-1, which recognises the α4β7 integrin heterodimer.

tagline: Gut-selective α4β7 integrin blocker for ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease
summary: Vedolizumab is a humanised monoclonal antibody that blocks the α4β7 integrin on gut-homing lymphocytes. By preventing these cells from entering intestinal tissue, it treats ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease with little systemic immunosuppression.
mechanism: The α4β7 integrin on memory T lymphocytes binds MAdCAM-1, an adhesion molecule expressed mainly on intestinal venules, directing those cells to the gut.

Vedolizumab binds the α4β7 heterodimer and blocks this interaction, reducing lymphocyte trafficking into the inflamed intestine. It does not block α4β1–VCAM-1 binding, so brain lymphocyte surveillance is preserved and PML risk is far lower than with natalizumab.

history.title: GEMINI trials
history.detail: Phase 3 GEMINI 1 and 2 results show efficacy in UC and Crohn's disease.

history.title: FDA and EU approval
history.detail: Approved in May in both the US and EU.

history.title: VARSITY
history.detail: Vedolizumab is superior to adalimumab for clinical remission in UC, the first head-to-head biologic trial in IBD.

history.title: EU subcutaneous form
history.detail: EU approves subcutaneous vedolizumab for maintenance.

history.title: US subcutaneous form
history.detail: FDA approves subcutaneous Entyvio for UC; Crohn's disease follows in 2024.

pk.metabolism: Proteolytic catabolism to peptides and amino acids (no CYP metabolism)
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody; cleared by catabolism and target-mediated uptake

serious: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (theoretical risk; not clearly established)

facts: VARSITY (2019) was the first head-to-head trial of two biologics in inflammatory bowel disease.
Its gut selectivity comes from MAdCAM-1 being expressed mainly in the intestine.
